t: Fine-Tuning: Teaching Pretrained Models New Tricks
title: Fine-Tuning: Teaching Pretrained Models New Tricks
description: Fine-tuning takes a pretrained model and continues training on a smaller, task-specific dataset, adjusting the weights toward the new domain. Full fine-tuning updates every parameter, which is powerful but expensive and risks catastrophic forgetting of the base capabilities.
content:
Fine-tuning takes a pretrained model and continues training on a smaller, task-specific dataset, adjusting the weights toward the new domain. Full fine-tuning updates every parameter, which is powerful but expensive and risks catastrophic forgetting of the base capabilities.

The practice is governed by learning-rate discipline: rates far below pretraining, warmup schedules, and early stopping on a validation split. Done well, a few thousand examples can specialize a general model into a domain expert.

Fine-tuning is the baseline upgrade against which all parameter-efficient methods are measured. Its cost profile is what motivated the entire adapter and LoRA literature.
key_facts: Continues training on task-specific data with low learning rates
Full fine-tuning updates all parameters; risks forgetting
Warmup, low LR, and early stopping are the core discipline
Baseline that parameter-efficient methods try to beat

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
description: LoRA freezes the pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank matrices into each layer: the update is factored as B times A with inner dimension r far smaller than the layer width. A 4096-wide layer with r=16 trains about 0.4% of the parameters of full fine-tuning.
content:
LoRA freezes the pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank matrices into each layer: the update is factored as B times A with inner dimension r far smaller than the layer width. A 4096-wide layer with r=16 trains about 0.4% of the parameters of full fine-tuning.

At inference the adapter merges into the base weights, so there is no latency cost, and swapping adapters swaps skills. Rank, alpha scaling, and target modules are the knobs; higher rank captures more complex adaptations.

LoRA made model customization a laptop-scale activity and is the standard mechanism behind the open-weights fine-tune ecosystem.
key_facts: Freezes base weights; trains low-rank update matrices
r=16 on 4096-wide layer trains ~0.4% of parameters
Adapters merge at inference: zero latency cost
Standard mechanism of the open fine-tune ecosystem

t: Model Merging: SLERP, TIES, and DARE
title: Model Merging: SLERP, TIES, and DARE
description: Model merging combines two or more fine-tuned models without further training: spherical interpolation (SLERP) walks the great-circle path between weight vectors, while TIES resolves sign conflicts and DARE sparsifies the deltas before adding them.
content:
Model merging combines two or more fine-tuned models without further training: spherical interpolation (SLERP) walks the great-circle path between weight vectors, while TIES resolves sign conflicts and DARE sparsifies the deltas before adding them.

The surprise is how well it works: merging a chat-tuned model with a math-tuned model often yields competence at both, because fine-tunes from the same base live in a shared loss basin. The merge is arithmetic on weights, yet the capability composition is real.

Merging turned the model hub into a combinatorial playground where capabilities are mixed like paint, and the best merges are found by evolutionary search over merge recipes.
key_facts: Combines fine-tunes with weight arithmetic, no retraining
SLERP interpolates along the great circle between models
TIES/DARE resolve conflicts and sparsify deltas
Works because sibling fine-tunes share a loss basin

t: Knowledge Distillation: Big Teacher, Small Student
title: Knowledge Distillation: Big Teacher, Small Student
description: Distillation trains a small student model to mimic a large teacher's outputs, including the soft probability distributions that reveal how the teacher generalizes. The student learns the teacher's dark knowledge, the relative confidences across wrong answers, not just the labels.
content:
Distillation trains a small student model to mimic a large teacher's outputs, including the soft probability distributions that reveal how the teacher generalizes. The student learns the teacher's dark knowledge, the relative confidences across wrong answers, not just the labels.

Temperature scaling softens the teacher's logits so the student sees the full ranking of alternatives. The result is routinely a model ten times smaller at ninety-plus percent of the teacher's capability.

Distillation is how frontier capability reaches phones and browsers: the giant model teaches, the small model ships.
key_facts: Student mimics teacher's soft output distributions
Temperature scaling reveals ranking among wrong answers
10x smaller models routinely keep 90%+ capability
How frontier models reach edge devices

title: Continual Learning Without Forgetting
description: Neural networks trained sequentially tend to overwrite old skills, catastrophic forgetting, because gradient descent has no memory of previous tasks. Continual learning methods fight this with rehearsal buffers, elastic weight consolidation, and parameter isolation.
content:
Neural networks trained sequentially tend to overwrite old skills, catastrophic forgetting, because gradient descent has no memory of previous tasks. Continual learning methods fight this with rehearsal buffers, elastic weight consolidation, and parameter isolation.

EWC protects important weights by penalizing movement in proportion to their Fisher-information importance for old tasks. Rehearsal simply replays stored old examples interleaved with new ones, the most reliable method in practice.

True lifelong learning remains open: current methods slow forgetting rather than eliminating it, and the benchmark suites keep getting harder.
key_facts: Sequential training overwrites old skills: catastrophic forgetting
EWC penalizes moving weights important to old tasks
Rehearsal buffers: replay old examples with new ones
Slows forgetting; full lifelong learning still open

t: RLHF and RLAIF: Aligning with Feedback
title: RLHF and RLAIF: Aligning with Feedback
description: Reinforcement learning from human feedback trains a reward model on human preference rankings, then optimizes the language model against that reward with PPO or DPO. The model learns which responses humans prefer, not just which are likely.
content:
Reinforcement learning from human feedback trains a reward model on human preference rankings, then optimizes the language model against that reward with PPO or DPO. The model learns which responses humans prefer, not just which are likely.

RLAIF replaces human labelers with AI critics applying a constitution of principles, scaling the feedback far beyond human labeling budgets. DPO simplified the pipeline by optimizing preferences directly without a separate reward model.

The method visibly improved helpfulness and harmlessness, and its failure modes, reward hacking and sycophancy, are now central alignment research topics.
key_facts: Reward model learns human preferences; policy optimizes against it
RLAIF scales feedback with AI critics and a constitution
DPO optimizes preferences without a separate reward model
Failure modes: reward hacking, sycophancy

title: Quantization: Smaller Weights, Same Brain
description: Quantization stores weights at lower precision, 8-bit integers or 4-bit floats instead of 32-bit, shrinking models 4-8x with small accuracy loss. The trick is calibration: measuring activation ranges so the reduced grid covers what matters.
content:
Quantization stores weights at lower precision, 8-bit integers or 4-bit floats instead of 32-bit, shrinking models 4-8x with small accuracy loss. The trick is calibration: measuring activation ranges so the reduced grid covers what matters.

GPTQ and AWQ quantize layer by layer, compensating each layer's error before moving on, which preserves quality at aggressive bit rates. Outlier-aware schemes keep a few sensitive weights at high precision.

Quantization is why 70-billion-parameter models run on single workstations: the brain stays the same, the suitcase gets smaller.
key_facts: 4-bit/8-bit weights shrink models 4-8x
Calibration maps the reduced grid to real activation ranges
GPTQ/AWQ quantize layer by layer with error compensation
Outlier-aware schemes protect sensitive weights

t: Adapters: Pluggable Skills for Frozen Models
title: Adapters: Pluggable Skills for Frozen Models
description: Adapter modules insert small trainable bottleneck layers between frozen transformer blocks: down-project, nonlinearity, up-project, with a residual skip. Only the adapters train, typically 1-3% of parameters per task.
content:
Adapter modules insert small trainable bottleneck layers between frozen transformer blocks: down-project, nonlinearity, up-project, with a residual skip. Only the adapters train, typically 1-3% of parameters per task.

Because the base never changes, one model serves many adapters, each a pluggable skill switched at request time. AdapterFusion even learns to combine adapters for multi-task inference.

Adapters were the first practical answer to multi-tenant serving: one giant frozen brain, thousands of tiny skill cartridges.
key_facts: Bottleneck layers inserted between frozen blocks
1-3% of parameters train per task; base untouched
One model serves many switched skills
AdapterFusion composes adapters for multi-task use

t: Mixture of Experts: Sparse Giant Models
title: Mixture of Experts: Sparse Giant Models
description: Mixture-of-experts models hold dozens of expert subnetworks and route each token to only the top one or two, so total parameters can reach trillions while active compute stays modest. The router learns which expert handles which inputs.
content:
Mixture-of-experts models hold dozens of expert subnetworks and route each token to only the top one or two, so total parameters can reach trillions while active compute stays modest. The router learns which expert handles which inputs.

Load balancing is the engineering challenge: without auxiliary losses, the router collapses onto a few experts and the rest atrophy. Expert choice and capacity factors keep the distribution healthy.

MoE is how the largest open models scale: more total knowledge, same per-token cost.
key_facts: Many experts; each token visits only top-1 or top-2
Trillions of parameters at modest active compute
Auxiliary losses prevent router collapse
Scales knowledge without scaling per-token cost

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
description: RAG upgrades a model without touching its weights: a retriever fetches relevant documents into the context window, and the model reasons over fresh, cited evidence. The knowledge cutoff problem disappears because the index, not the weights, holds the facts.
content:
RAG upgrades a model without touching its weights: a retriever fetches relevant documents into the context window, and the model reasons over fresh, cited evidence. The knowledge cutoff problem disappears because the index, not the weights, holds the facts.

Dense retrievers embed queries and passages into a shared vector space, and approximate nearest-neighbor indexes serve millions of passages in milliseconds. Chunking strategy and reranking decide answer quality more than model size does.

RAG turned enterprise AI from retraining projects into indexing projects, and citations made the outputs auditable.
key_facts: Retriever fetches documents; model reasons over evidence
Dense embeddings plus ANN index serve millions of passages
Chunking and reranking matter more than model size
Citations make outputs auditable

title: Evaluating Upgrades: Benchmarks That Matter
description: An upgrade is only real if measured: MMLU and its harder successors test broad knowledge, HumanEval tests code, GSM8K tests math reasoning, and arena-style human voting captures qualities benchmarks miss. Good evaluation uses held-out sets the model never trained on.
content:
An upgrade is only real if measured: MMLU and its harder successors test broad knowledge, HumanEval tests code, GSM8K tests math reasoning, and arena-style human voting captures qualities benchmarks miss. Good evaluation uses held-out sets the model never trained on.

Contamination is the constant threat: benchmark text leaks into training data and scores inflate. Live benchmarks with fresh questions, and canary strings that detect memorization, are the current defenses.

The discipline is simple to state and hard to practice: decide the metric before the upgrade, and distrust any number you wanted to see.
key_facts: MMLU, HumanEval, GSM8K cover knowledge, code, math
Arena voting captures qualities benchmarks miss
Contamination inflates scores; live benchmarks defend
Fix metrics before upgrading; distrust wanted numbers

title: Catastrophic Forgetting: The Core Obstacle
description: A network trained on task B after task A typically collapses on A, because gradient descent optimizes only the current loss landscape. The weights that encoded A are overwritten without ceremony; the network has no declarative memory of what it used to know.
content:
A network trained on task B after task A typically collapses on A, because gradient descent optimizes only the current loss landscape. The weights that encoded A are overwritten without ceremony; the network has no declarative memory of what it used to know.

This is why every upgrade method carries a forgetting tax, and why rehearsal, the bluntest method, still wins most comparisons. Biological brains avoid it with systems consolidation; artificial ones have no equivalent yet.

Solving forgetting is arguably the upgrade problem: an AI that could truly accumulate skills would not need most upgrade machinery.
key_facts: New training overwrites old skills without ceremony
Every upgrade method pays a forgetting tax
Rehearsal still beats fancier methods in practice
Accumulative learning would obsolete much upgrade machinery

title: Scaling Laws: Predictable Returns
description: Scaling laws found that language-model loss falls as a power law in parameters, data, and compute, letting labs predict a large run's quality from small experiments. The Chinchilla analysis corrected the balance: many models were undertrained, and equal scaling of parameters and tokens is compute-optimal.
content:
Scaling laws found that language-model loss falls as a power law in parameters, data, and compute, letting labs predict a large run's quality from small experiments. The Chinchilla analysis corrected the balance: many models were undertrained, and equal scaling of parameters and tokens is compute-optimal.

These laws turned training into budgeting: given a compute allowance, the optimal model size and token count are computable in advance. Inference-time scaling, spending compute on reasoning at query time, is the newer frontier.

Predictability is the laws' real gift: capability planning became engineering instead of gambling.
key_facts: Loss falls as a power law in params, data, compute
Chinchilla: scale tokens and parameters equally
Compute budgets map to optimal size in advance
Inference-time scaling is the newer frontier

title: The Open-Weights Ecosystem
description: Open-weights releases turned model upgrading into a public science: anyone can fine-tune, merge, quantize, and benchmark, and the best recipes propagate within days. The hub model counts fine-tunes in the hundreds of thousands.
content:
Open-weights releases turned model upgrading into a public science: anyone can fine-tune, merge, quantize, and benchmark, and the best recipes propagate within days. The hub model counts fine-tunes in the hundreds of thousands.

This openness accelerated every technique on this list, because each is testable by thousands of independent practitioners. It also moved safety work into the open, where failures are found faster.

The ecosystem's norm is publish the weights, publish the recipe, publish the evals: upgrade science as a commons.
key_facts: Hundreds of thousands of public fine-tunes and merges
Techniques improve through mass independent testing
Safety failures surface faster in the open
Norm: weights, recipe, and evals all published

title: Upgrade Safety: Capability Without Harm
description: Every upgrade that adds capability also moves the risk surface: a more helpful model is a more useful tool for misuse, and fine-tuning can strip safety training faster than it was added. Safety evaluation must therefore ride along with capability evaluation.
content:
Every upgrade that adds capability also moves the risk surface: a more helpful model is a more useful tool for misuse, and fine-tuning can strip safety training faster than it was added. Safety evaluation must therefore ride along with capability evaluation.

Current practice includes refusal benchmarks, jailbreak test suites, and capability-threshold policies that gate the most sensitive upgrades. The research frontier is unlearning, surgically removing dangerous knowledge while keeping everything else.

The standing rule is proportionality: the stronger the upgrade, the stronger the safety case required before deployment.
key_facts: Capability gains move the risk surface too
Fine-tuning can strip safety training quickly
Refusal benchmarks and jailbreak suites ride along
Proportionality: stronger upgrades need stronger safety cases

t: From Upgrade to Autonomy: Where It Leads
title: From Upgrade to Autonomy: Where It Leads
description: The arc of upgrade techniques points toward self-improving systems: models that fine-tune themselves on their own outputs, merge their own variants, and distill their own successors. Early versions of each loop already exist in research.
content:
The arc of upgrade techniques points toward self-improving systems: models that fine-tune themselves on their own outputs, merge their own variants, and distill their own successors. Early versions of each loop already exist in research.

The honest assessment is that the loops work but compound errors as well as capabilities, which is why verification machinery, benchmarks, critics, and human oversight, scales with the automation rather than shrinking.

The destination is not a single upgrade but an upgrade discipline: measure, improve, verify, repeat, with the verification as automated as the improvement.
key_facts: Self-fine-tuning, self-merging, self-distillation loops exist
Loops compound errors as well as capabilities
Verification must scale with automation
The discipline: measure, improve, verify, repeat
